To find the **greatest common divisor (GCD)** of the numbers $ 3339 $, $ 2961 $, and $ 1491 $, we use the **Euclidean algorithm**, which is an efficient method for computing the GCD of two or more integers.

---

### Step 1: Find GCD of $ 3339 $ and $ 2961 $

We apply the Euclidean algorithm:

$$
\begin{align*}
3339 \div 2961 &= 1 \text{ remainder } 378 \\
2961 \div 378 &= 7 \text{ remainder } 315 \\
378 \div 315 &= 1 \text{ remainder } 63 \\
315 \div 63 &= 5 \text{ remainder } 0 \\
\end{align*}
$$

So, $ \gcd(3339, 2961) = 63 $.

---

### Step 2: Find GCD of $ 63 $ and $ 1491 $

$$
\begin{align*}
1491 \div 63 &= 23 \text{ remainder } 42 \\
63 \div 42 &= 1 \text{ remainder } 21 \\
42 \div 21 &= 2 \text{ remainder } 0 \\
\end{align*}
$$

So, $ \gcd(63, 1491) = 21 $.

---

### Final Step: GCD of all three numbers

Since the GCD of $ 3339 $ and $ 2961 $ is $ 63 $, and the GCD of $ 63 $ and $ 1491 $ is $ 21 $, the GCD of all three numbers is:

$$
\boxed{21}
$$
